parts.working_md:
$\text{Product}=\dfrac{3}{2}\times\dfrac{4}{3}\times\dfrac{5}{4}\times\cdots\times\dfrac{n}{n-1}\times\dfrac{n+1}{n}=\dfrac{n+1}{2}$

The product will be an integer value when $n+1$ is divisible by $2$, i.e. $n\in\{3\,;\,5\,;\,7\,;\,\dots\}$

Therefore, $n$ must be an odd number, greater than $2$.

For $n=5$ the product is $\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)=3$

$n\in\{3\,;\,5\,;\,7\,;\,\dots\}$
